text:
Marathon Petroleum edged up 0.42% today to $399.44, continuing a sharp nine-day rally that has now gained 12.6% since early September. The move reflects sustained strength in crude oil prices, which hit $101 per barrel (Brent) on escalating U.S.-Iran tensions and Middle East supply concerns. Refineries are running at 98% capacity—near maximum—which means Marathon and peers capture more profit margin when oil and fuel prices stay elevated; the company also benefits directly from higher crude as it moves through the refining system.

The broader context here is geopolitical. Fears of supply disruptions from Persian Gulf conflict have kept oil prices well above $90 (U.S. crude at $91.48), and that elevated price floor appears to be holding the refining sector higher even as the stock has already moved significantly in two weeks. Storage levels for gasoline and diesel remain moderate, which leaves less downward pressure on fuel prices and supports refiner margins.
